title: Westfall
body: Westfall was the breadbasket of Stormwind, a broad country of golden fields and windmills between Elwynn and the Great Sea. That plenty is gone. The Defias Brotherhood has seized or burned farm after farm, taken the mines and quarries and hired the Riverpaw gnolls, and harvest golems stalk the empty fields. The crown withdrew its soldiers rather than bear the cost of keeping them here, and those who stayed feel abandoned. At Sentinel Hill the farmers have raised a militia of their own.

title: Saldean's Farm
body: Saldean's Farm, north of Sentinel Hill, is one of the very few homesteads in Westfall still worked by its owners. While neighbor after neighbor fled, among them Theodore and Verna Furlbrow, who got no farther than a broken wagon on the northern road, Farmer Saldean swore no band of thieves would drive him off his land. His wife Salma keeps the kitchen busy, and harvest watchers trample the fields around them.

parts.body: Their stubbornness paid the militia back. A thief caught stealing the Saldeans' wagon bought his life by offering to lead the militia to the Brotherhood's secret hideout.

title: Sentinel Hill
body: The stone tower on Sentinel Hill is the headquarters of the People's Militia, raised by Gryan Stoutmantle from farmers who lost their land and volunteers willing to fight beside them. Recruits earn their place against the Defias before they are sworn in under the Light. Help from the crown is scarce: the quartermaster buys armor through a contact in Stormwind's Old Town and has it flown in, for the capital seems to have all but forgotten this land.
sources: quest 109 description (stone tower on Sentinel Hill)

title: Alexston Farmstead
body: West of Sentinel Hill stand the burned ruins of the Alexston Farmstead, picked over by Defias pillagers. The boy who grew up working these fields became Baros Alexston, City Architect of Stormwind, and when the thieves came his father could save little of what the family owned. A few keepsakes are said to lie hidden on the property still.

parts.body: Baros and Edwin VanCleef were fellow Stonemasons as young men, rebuilding Stormwind side by side, and the Kingpin carried an unsent letter to his old comrade to the end.
sources: quest 399 description (Baros Alexston, farm west of Sentinel Hill burned and taken by thieves)

title: Moonbrook
body: Moonbrook was a mining town and the heart of the southern farmlands, with its own mayor and even a schoolhouse for the farm children. Its townsfolk are long gone. The Defias Brotherhood holds its streets now, and a Defias profiteer sells his wares to anyone who will buy.

parts.body: Beneath one of its barns lies the hidden entrance to the Deadmines, where the Brotherhood keeps its true hideout out of the militia's sight.

title: The Cooper Residence
body: On the western side of Moonbrook stands the empty house of the Cooper family, who made barrels for the townsfolk and even for a few buyers in Stormwind. A dusty journal left inside is half ledger and half diary, in which Mr. Cooper wrote of handing the trade down to his younger brother.

parts.body: At the Argent Tournament in Icecrown a champion called the Black Knight claims descent from the Coopers of Westfall, and every rider set to face him has met an untimely end.
The journal names no heir, and the trade passed to Cooper's brother. The tournament's officials now think the Black Knight's tale a sham, and watch him quietly.

title: Westfall Lighthouse
body: At the southern end of the coast a lighthouse warns ships off the rocks. Its keeper's family is dead. Old Murk-Eye's murlocs first frightened them away and left the light dark, and Captain Grayson's ship struck the rocks that night. When the family came back to rekindle it, the murlocs returned and killed them while his ghost looked on. Since then the dead captain has tended the flame himself, so that no other sailor shares his fate.

parts.body: Old Murk-Eye is dead. It cannot undo the keeper's family's deaths or his own, Grayson says, but the sea is a little safer each night the flame burns.

title: Gryan Stoutmantle
body: Born in Westfall, Gryan Stoutmantle went north as a knight of the Silver Hand and fought on the battlefields of Lordaeron. He came home to find the farms of his youth overrun by thieves and the crown unwilling to defend them, and rather than turn his back on the people who stayed, he founded the People's Militia.

parts.body: When the Alliance went to war in Northrend, Stoutmantle took his men north as the Westfall Brigade, sent to find a road into the north and secure resources for the king, and he commands their camp in the Grizzly Hills.

sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Gryan_Stoutmantle (born in Westfall, Knight of the Silver Hand, founded the Militia, Westfall Brigade)

title: Edwin VanCleef
body: Edwin VanCleef was guildmaster of the Stonemasons, the craftsmen who rebuilt Stormwind after the First War, and in his youth a peerless fighter. When the nobles refused to pay what the guild was owed, he turned down a government post out of loyalty to his masons, led a riot in the city and fled, swearing revenge. Gryan Stoutmantle, who knew the name, could hardly believe so talented a man had turned scoundrel.

parts.body: The Brotherhood's own messenger proved it: VanCleef gives the orders. His followers call him the Defias Kingpin, and he has drawn gnolls, kobolds and even goblins to his cause.

sources: quest 373 reward text (peerless fighter, revenge has consumed him)
